source_text: SEXTUM, De essentia, & nominibus Dei in specie. Essentia Dei est natura singularis, tribus personis communis. Dicitur etiam μορφὴ Θεοῦ, forma Dei, Phil. 2.6. Etsi enim οὐσία, φύσις & μορφή, h. e. essentia, natura & forma de Philosophorum sententia differunt: tamen secundum sanctos patres in doctrina de Deo, haec tria idem sunt, teste Damasceno in Isagoge cap. 1. Essentia, natura & forma, secundum sanctos patres, idem sunt. Itemque divinitas, Rom. 1.20. Est singularis, quia numero ita est una, ut simul sit unica, Deut. 4.35. Est communis, quia aequaliter est trium personarum, 1 Joh. 5.7.
english: CHAPTER SIX. On the essence and names of God in particular.

The essence of God is a singular nature, common to the three persons. It is also called the form of God (Philippians 2:6). For although essence, nature, and form differ in the philosophers' judgment, yet according to the holy fathers in the doctrine of God these three are the same, as Damascene testifies in the Isagoge, chapter 1. Likewise also divinity (Romans 1:20). It is singular, because numerically it is so one that it is at once unique (Deuteronomy 4:35). It is common, because it equally belongs to the three persons (1 John 5:7).

source_text: NONUM est ex novo testamento: ὁ Θεός, Deus. DECIMUM est Κύριος, DOMINUS, Matth. passim. XIII. Haec est praecipuorum Dei nominum recensio & usus. Etsi nullum nomen Dei infinitam essentiam perfecte exprimat: tamen multa sunt ejus nomina, quae ipsius proprietates imprimunt. Deus enim verbo suo multa de se revelavit. Nomina a Deo in Scripturis imposita utiliter notitiam Dei augent; ab hominibus conficta nomina non facile admittenda. Cap. 6 closes before Cap. 7 De attributis Dei.
english: NINTH from the New Testament is ho Theos, God. TENTH is Kyrios, LORD (Matthew everywhere).

XIII. This is the review and use of the chief names of God. Although no name of God perfectly expresses the infinite essence: yet many are His names which impress His properties. For God by His Word has revealed many things about Himself. Names imposed by God in the Scriptures usefully increase the knowledge of God; names invented by men are not easily to be admitted.

source_text: REGULA. 1. Deus ita est unus, ut sit unicus, nec habeat multas essentias. Ratio prioris est, quia fieri non potest, ut plura sint prima sive summa & infinita principia. Ratio posterioris est, quia Deus per unam eandemque essentiam est immutabilis, aeternus, sapiens, bonus, omnipotens. Quapropter Deus non habet multas essentias diversas vel adversas, intensas vel remissas, substantiales vel accidentales, genericas & specificam, totales vel partiales: sed essentiam ita unam numero seu individuam, ut non admittat principium individuationis. 2. Essentia Dei est communis tribus personis: non tamen est una genere vel specie. Neque enim multiplicatur in personis, ut res universalis: sed aequaliter est in singulis ut res singularis infinita. 3. Multitudo attributorum Dei non pugnat cum unitate essentiae Dei; quia omnia ista attributa sunt unum in essentia. Nihil enim sunt aliud, quam una eademque Dei essentia relata ad varia objecta & effecta. Sic aeternitas Dei est ipsa Dei essentia, quatenus non habet initium, successionem & finem durationis. Omnipotentia Dei est ipsa Dei essentia, quatenus efficere potest omne bonum.
english: RULE. 1. God is so one that He is unique, and does not have many essences. The reason of the former is that it cannot happen that there be several first or highest and infinite principles. The reason of the latter is that God through one and the same essence is immutable, eternal, wise, good, omnipotent. Therefore God does not have many essences diverse or opposed, intense or remiss, substantial or accidental, generic and specific, total or partial: but an essence so one in number or individual that it does not admit a principle of individuation.

2. The essence of God is common to the three persons: yet it is not one in genus or species. For it is not multiplied in the persons as a universal thing: but equally is in each as an infinite singular thing. 3. The multitude of God's attributes does not fight with the unity of God's essence; because all those attributes are one in essence. For they are nothing other than one and the same essence of God related to various objects and effects. So God's eternity is God's very essence insofar as it has no beginning, succession, and end of duration. God's omnipotence is God's very essence insofar as it can effect every good.

source_text: XI. Septimo, quaedam sunt concreta, ut Deus, Dominus, Pater: quaedam abstracta, ut vita, charitas, deitas. Illa docent, Deum esse vere subsistentem: haec vero eum esse ens simplicissimum. XII. Atque haec est nominum divinorum distinctio. PRIMUM est יהוה. Exod. 15.3; Psal. 83.19; Esai. passim. Hoc nomen Tetragrammaton & Schemhamphoras etiam dicitur. Literae, utpote quantitates, sive pictae sive pronunciatae, per se nullius sunt efficaciae. Nomen MT' sive Tetragrammaton sive Schemhamphoras nec miraculosum nec magicam vim habet.
english: XI. Seventh, some are concrete, as God, Lord, Father: some abstract, as life, charity, deity. Those teach that God truly subsists: but these that He is a most simple being. XII. And this is the distinction of the divine names.

FIRST is YHWH (Exodus 15:3; Psalm 83:19; Isaiah everywhere). This name is also called the Tetragrammaton and Schemhamphoras. Letters, as quantities, whether painted or pronounced, of themselves have no efficacy. The name YHWH or Tetragrammaton or Schemhamphoras has neither miraculous nor magical force.

source_text: SECUNDUM nomen est JAH, Exod. 15.2; Psal. passim, quo se invicem ad DEUM laudandum exhortabantur. TERTIUM est EHEJE, Exod. 3.13.14, denotans absolutam Dei exsistentiam & necessitatem. QUARTUM nomen est EL, Esai. 9.6, significans fortitudinem & potentiam Dei.
english: The SECOND name is JAH (Exodus 15:2; Psalms everywhere), by which they exhorted one another to praise GOD. The THIRD is EHEJE (Exodus 3:13-14), denoting God's absolute existence and necessity. The FOURTH name is EL (Isaiah 9:6), signifying God's fortitude and power.

source_text: II. In essentia DEI consideranda sunt nomina & attributa divina. Multi veteres & juniores nomina & attributa Dei pro iisdem capiunt, ita ut attributa sive proprietates Dei essentiales etiam appellent nomina. At, cum nos proprietati vocum studere debeamus, nomina Dei ab attributis sive proprietatibus essentialibus hic distinguere maluimus. III. Nomina divina sunt, quibus Deus in sacris literis appellatur, ut iis, quantum nostra refert, natura illius explicetur. Nomen Dei in scripturis varia significat. Primo, notam, qua Deus designatur & a creaturis discernitur, Gen. 32.29; Exod. 3.15 & 14.5. Secundo, Deum ipsum, Deut. 28; Psal. 5.12 & 7.18 & 20.2 & 116.4; Prov. 18.10. Tertio, potentiam & gratiam Dei, Psal. 118.10.11.12. Quarto, voluntatem & mandatum Dei, Deut. 18.19; 1 Sam. 17.45; Joh. 5.43; Luc. 24.47. Quinto, cultum, invocationem, celebrationem, professionem Dei ac fidem, Mich. 4.5; Matth. 28.19; Act. 21.13. Nos in prima significatione hic accipimus.
english: II. In the essence of GOD the divine names and attributes are to be considered. Many ancients and moderns take the names and attributes of God for the same, so that they also call the essential attributes or properties of God names. But since we ought to study the propriety of words, we preferred here to distinguish the names of God from the essential attributes or properties.

III. Divine names are those by which God is called in the sacred letters, that by them, as far as concerns us, His nature may be explained. The name of God in the Scriptures signifies various things. First, a mark by which God is designated and discerned from creatures (Genesis 32:29; Exodus 3:15 and 14:5). Second, God Himself (Deuteronomy 28; Psalm 5:12 and 7:18 and 20:2 and 116:4; Proverbs 18:10). Third, the power and grace of God (Psalm 118:10-12). Fourth, the will and commandment of God (Deuteronomy 18:19; 1 Samuel 17:45; John 5:43; Luke 24:47). Fifth, the worship, invocation, celebration, profession of God and faith (Micah 4:5; Matthew 28:19; Acts 21:13). We take it here in the first signification.

source_text: IV. Est autem nominum divinorum notanda distinctio, praecipuorum recensio, omnium usus. V. Distinctio eorum est multiplex. Primo, quaedam divina nomina sunt in veteri testamento, quaedam in novo. Illa fere sunt Jah, Eheje, El, Elohim, Schaddai, Adonai, Heljon &c. haec Θεός, Κύριος, Πατήρ, Υἱός, Abba, Πνεῦμα, Σαβαώθ. VI. Secundo, alia notant essentiam Dei, alia essentiae proprietates. Illa sunt Jah, Eheje & similia: haec vero El, Elohim, Schaddai &c. VII. Tertio, quaedam soli Deo proprie conveniunt, ut Jehovah: quaedam communia sunt Deo & creaturis, sed diversa ratione, ut Elohim. Illa discernunt Deum ab omnibus rebus creatis, quatenus perfectiones Dei prorsus incommunicabiles notant: haec vero declarant, eum omnis boni naturae auctorem, quippe quae de Deo & creaturis analogice praedicantur. VIII. Quarto, quaedam ex illis sunt absoluta, ut Deus omnipotens: quaedam respectiva, eaque vel ad personas divinas, ut Pater, Filius, Spiritus sanctus, vel ad res creatas, ut creator, servator, Rex regum, Dominus dominantium. IX. Quinto, quaedam sunt affirmativa, ut omnipotens, quaedam negativa, ut infinitus.
english: IV. But of the divine names a distinction is to be noted, a review of the chief ones, and the use of all. V. Their distinction is multiplex. First, some divine names are in the Old Testament, some in the New. Those are for the most part Jah, Eheje, El, Elohim, Schaddai, Adonai, Heljon, etc.; these Theos, Kyrios, Father, Son, Abba, Spirit, Sabaoth.

VI. Second, some note God's essence, others properties of the essence. Those are Jah, Eheje and the like: but these El, Elohim, Schaddai, etc. VII. Third, some properly belong to God alone, as Jehovah: some are common to God and creatures, but by a diverse ratio, as Elohim. Those discern God from all created things insofar as they note God's altogether incommunicable perfections: but these declare Him the author of every good nature, since they are predicated of God and creatures analogically.

VIII. Fourth, some of them are absolute, as God omnipotent: some respective, and that either toward the divine persons, as Father, Son, Holy Spirit, or toward created things, as creator, savior, King of kings, Lord of lords. IX. Fifth, some are affirmative, as omnipotent, some negative, as infinite.

source_text: QUINTUM est ELOHIM, Gen. 1.1 & infinitis locis. Interdum denotat omnes tres personas Deitatis. SEXTUM nomen est Adonai, Dan. 9.17; Psal. passim. SEPTIMUM est Schaddai, Gen. 17.1, ὁ παντοκράτωρ. OCTAVUM est HELJON, Psal. 9.2 &c.
english: FIFTH is ELOHIM (Genesis 1:1 and in countless places). Sometimes it denotes all three persons of the Deity. The SIXTH name is Adonai (Daniel 9:17; Psalms everywhere). SEVENTH is Schaddai (Genesis 17:1), the Almighty. EIGHTH is HELJON (Psalm 9:2 etc.).
